text:
Maya: Quick question — we need a playbook for SLO-driven routing across tiers/regions. Currently fallback to quantized variants fires too aggressively in EU-west during bursts. Thoughts on thresholds + CB cooldowns + console controls? :thinking:

Liam: Agreed. We should have a default per-tier latency SLO + two thresholds: warn (p95 > x) and trip (p95 > y). Warn triggers telemetry alert, trip starts circuit-breaker and fallback to compatible model variant.

Liam: Example policy snippet:
```yaml
routing_policy:
  tiers:
    - name: enterprise
      slo_p95_ms: 120
      warn_threshold: 1.25
      trip_threshold: 1.6
      cb_cooldown_s: 300
      fallback_sequence: ["base-opt-q4", "base-opt-q8"]
    - name: standard
      slo_p95_ms: 250
      warn_threshold: 1.35
      trip_threshold: 2.0
      cb_cooldown_s: 180
      fallback_sequence: ["base-opt-q8"]
```

Rafael: Important: avoid immediate trips on a single noisy host. Use rolling window + min sample size. Also add hysteresis to prevent flip-flop. Metrics we need: route_p95_ms, sample_count, cb_state, fallback_success_rate.

Jen (oncall): real incident last month — CB flipped in ca-central for a customer because p95 spiked for 2 mins due to noisy batch, fallback lowered quality and customer sent an alert. We need manual override and "suspend fallback" toggle per-customer.

Alex (ui): Console UX idea: show live predicted latency impact if you enable a fallback policy (estimate from last 24h). Offer quick actions: preview, enable (canary 5/25/100), emergency rollback. Keep the policy DSL hidden in advanced mode.

Sophia (pm): +1 on canary percentages. Also audit logs for each automatic fallback decision and who/what changed thresholds. We should expose RBAC: only SREs can change trip thresholds, PMs can propose.

ops-bot: IncidentBot: CB events past 30d: 18 trips, 7 manual overrides, 3 sustained rollbacks. (generated summary)

Rafael: Also debate: API shaping vs declarative policy. I prefer declarative policy stored per-customer with a “policy_version” field. API can be a thin controller that approves changes.

Liam: Implementation note: runtime should surface cb_state and last_trip_reason on the request trace so tracing + logs correlate with slow requests.

Maya: Action items: 1) Draft RFC with policy schema + cooldown/hysteresis rules (owner: Liam) 2) Instrumentation ticket for metrics/trace fields (owner: Rafael) 3) Console mockups for preview/canary/override (owner: Alex) 4) Run tabletop incident to validate playbook (owner: Jen). Can we have RFC by EOW? :eyes:

Alex (ui): I'll sketch mockups by Wed.

Jen (oncall): I'll prepare incident notes and examples.

Liam: RFC draft tonight, will ping for review.

Maya: Great — if we converge on schema we'll include it in the rollout checklist. :thumbsup:
